ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Approximately 45% high-intensity pixels (white) to 55% low-intensity pixels (black/dark-grey) across the visible ventral fluke surface.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Dominant high-intensity white fields are located on the distal halves of both lobes. A large, contiguous low-intensity dark field occupies the central region surrounding the notch and extends toward the base. Fine-grained dark mottling is present along the lower margins and at the transition between the dark central field and white distal tips.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep, acute V-shaped notch with an estimated pixel angle of approximately 45 to 50 degrees relative to the lobe intersection.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Extremely high-frequency and high-amplitude serrations are present along the entire continuous trailing edge; characterized by irregular, sharp-edged peaks and deep U-shaped valleys distinct from the surrounding water background.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: The leading edges exhibit a linear sweep with slight convexity as they transition toward the distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Multiple localized circular high-intensity pixel clusters (scars) are distributed primarily within the dark pigmented medial and proximal regions of both lobes.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Several distinct, parallel vertical linear pixel disruptions (rake marks) are visible in the central dark region and extending into the white field of the left lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive irregular trauma-induced notches and missing segments are visible across the trailing edge topography. Prominent vertical parallel rake marks suggest historical interaction with predators.
other_distinctive_markers: The trailing edge exhibits a unique 'saw-tooth' profile with unusually deep and frequent indentations compared to standard morphology.
